hero.title: Research Without Guessing.
hero.intro: Turn an important uncertainty into a research question. Record traceable sources, distinguish evidence from interpretation, and plan a check that could change your mind.

questions.prompt: What should a research log separate?
questions.explanation: Preserve what the source supports separately from your interpretation.

questions.prompt: Three articles repeat one report. What should you do?
options: Trace the original source; do not count them as independent confirmations
questions.explanation: Repeated reporting may come from one source.

questions.prompt: Evidence has not yet been collected. What belongs in the log?
options: A result you expect to see
A clearly labeled plan and source/check to pursue
questions.explanation: Plans are acceptable when kept separate from collected evidence.

scenes.title: Start with an uncertainty
scenes.visual: Founder reviews an anonymous journey map.
scenes.narration: Research begins with something you do not yet know. Choose one important uncertainty from your customer journey. Ask a specific question that could change your decision. Do not start by searching only for support for an idea you already want to build.

scenes.title: Match the method to the question
scenes.visual: Editable observation, conversation and document cards.
scenes.narration: An observation can show an action in a setting. A recent-experience conversation can reveal someone’s account. A document can describe a policy or a service. Each method has limits. A product page does not establish customer satisfaction, and a conversation does not by itself prove what happened.

scenes.title: Record a traceable source
scenes.visual: Editable source log with anonymous reference codes.
scenes.narration: For each entry, record the claim or question, what the source actually supports, the source reference and date, and its status. Use observed, reported, documented, inferred, assumed or planned. Keep private identities out of the log. If you have not collected evidence, record a plan rather than a result.

scenes.title: Separate evidence from inference
scenes.visual: Editable supported statement and interpretation cards.
scenes.narration: A visitor asked staff for directions is different from visitors hate the signs. The first can be a specific observation; the second is an interpretation requiring more evidence. Preserve the context, limitations and possible alternative explanations. Do not invent numbers or quotes to fill a gap.

scenes.title: Look for what could contradict you
scenes.narration: Seek information that could weaken your idea. Check relevance, recency, source proximity and possible bias. Three articles repeating the same report are not three independent confirmations. Record conflicts rather than forcing agreement. One account is not representative of a whole market.

scenes.title: Plan the next check
scenes.narration: Create your Research and Source Log with three sourced entries or clearly labeled plans. Separate supported statements from inferences and unknowns. Finish with a practical, ethical next check and a decision rule. Research improves your questions; completing this log does not validate demand.

blocks.prompt:
Create a beginner-friendly LYNQ Academy explainer plus evidence-log demo, Module 1.3 Lesson 13: Research Without Guessing. Editorial target 150 seconds, 16:9 1080p. Navy #0B2338, teal #087D79, mint #BCF2DF, white; contemporary Dubai workspace, diverse adult cast, clear friendly English narrator. Fictional anonymous examples only, labeled Illustrative example in post. Teach question/method fit, source traceability, observed/reported/documented/inferred/assumed/planned labels, independence, source limitations and disconfirming evidence. No fabricated citations, URLs, quotes, statistics, research outcomes or demand claims.

blocks.label: I read the transcript or reviewed the learning guide. Video is not required.

children: is information relevant to a question. An
is an interpretation you draw from it. A
is where information came from. Your research log must preserve the difference.
Useful for actions in a permitted setting. It does not reveal a person’s feelings or intentions by itself.
Useful for a person’s account. Recall, selection and question wording may affect the answer.
Useful for what the document describes. A product page is not evidence that customers are satisfied.
Not collected yet? Label the entry planned, with a source to seek. Never fabricate a reference or result.
Is the source relevant to your exact group, task and context?
What is its date, proximity to the event and possible bias?
Is it independent, or repeating another source?
What does it support, and what remains unknown?
What would contradict your preferred explanation?

“One visitor asked staff for directions” may support an observed interaction in one setting. It does not establish that signs failed, that visitors are frustrated, or that people will pay for a new app.

children: This log does not verify sources, establish representativeness or prove demand. Browser storage is plaintext; avoid private identities, confidential documents and credentials.
Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: Match the method to your question. Separate supported statements, inference and plans; check traceability and source limitations.
replies.guide: Write three source entries or honest collection plans. Record status, reference/date, support, interpretation and limits; seek disconfirming evidence.
replies.review: Research Log check: {missing} required fields still empty. This scripted check counts fields only; it cannot verify sources, independence, research results or demand.
replies.challenge: Are you seeking only confirmation? Are repeated articles independent? What does each source actually support? Have plans become invented results?

sections.label: 05 / CHALLENGE
sections.heading: Look for evidence against your story.

children: Are sources repeating the same account? Is the context relevant? Did you search only for support? Have planned entries become results? Can participants decline, and can notes stay anonymous?
Answer all three. You can retry; all three correct are required for local completion.
